newsitem.title: UK: Boots dips after OFT move on OTC medicines.
newsitem.headline: Boots dips after OFT move on OTC medicines.

text.p: Shares in retailing group Boots Company Plc retreated on Friday after the UK's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) said it would take legal action to remove resale price maintenance (RPM) on over-the-counter medicines.

The unexpected move sent shares in Boots 7-1/2p lower before they recovered to be down 2-1/2p at 641p, in early afternoon but analysts said the impact on Boots, which controls one of Britain's largest pharmacy chains, was likely to be limited.
RPM covers the fixing of retail prices of branded over-the-counter medicines such as painkillers and indigestion treatments.
Comparisons with WH Smith after the removal last year of the net book agreement suggested that Boots may turn out to be a beneficiary from the OFT's move said MeesPierson analyst Nick Bubb.
"Smiths got stronger, increasing market share through promotions and using muscle with suppliers. I expect the same will happen to Boots - it'll get bigger and stronger," he said.

"If pricing from ASDA and the food superstores was very aggressive we could see some impact on the bottom line but it won't be that big a deal. I suspect at the end of the day it'll have no impact (on Boots) whatsoever."

OFT head John Bridgeman said the removal of RPM could save consumers 180 million stg a year but the Community Pharmacy Action Group warned if the court backed the move, it could lead to the closure of thousands of Britain's pharmacies.
